method_card.title: Weather, Travel Problems and Transactions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers weather expressions in different tenses, common travel problems and transactional language at a tourist information office.

FrenchEnglish
il fait beauit's nice weather
il fait chaudit's hot
il fait froidit's cold
il fait mauvaisit's bad weather
il pleutit's raining
il neigeit's snowing
il y a du soleilit's sunny
il y a du ventit's windy
il y a des nuagesit's cloudy
j'ai perdu mon passeportI lost my passport
mon vol est annulémy flight is cancelled
je chercheI am looking for
des renseignementsinformation
une carte de la régiona map of the area
(Higher) il y aura(Higher) there will be

Weather in three tenses:

  • Present: il fait beau, il pleut, il y a du soleil
  • Imperfect (past description): il faisait chaud, il pleuvait, il y avait du vent
  • Near future: il va faire beau, il va pleuvoir, il va neiger
  • Simple future (Higher): il fera beau, il pleuvra, il y aura du soleil

Travel problem phrases: J'ai perdu mon passeport / mon portefeuille. (I have lost my passport / wallet.) Mon vol est annulé. (My flight is cancelled.) Je cherche l'office du tourisme. (I am looking for the tourist office.)

Model paragraph: L'été dernier, il faisait très chaud en France mais aujourd'hui il y a des nuages. Demain, il va pleuvoir. J'ai perdu mon portefeuille au marché et j'ai dû aller à l'office du tourisme pour chercher de l'aide. (Last summer, it was very hot in France but today it's cloudy. Tomorrow it's going to rain. I lost my wallet at the market and had to go to the tourist office to look for help.)
steps: Learn the two weather patterns: il fait + adjective and il y a + noun
Master weather in three tenses: present, imperfect (past description) and near future
Learn key travel problem phrases using past and present tenses
Practice transactional language for the tourist information office role-play

exam_context.frequency: Weather expressions appear in every exam series; tourist information is a prescribed speaking setting

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'En hiver, il fait froid et il neige à la montagne.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break it down: En hiver | il fait froid | et | il neige | à la montagne.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: En hiver = In winter. il fait froid = it's cold. il neige = it snows / it's snowing.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: In winter, it's cold and it snows in the mountains.

worked_examples.question: How do you change weather expressions from present to imperfect (past)?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: il fait → il faisait (it was). The imperfect stem of faire is fais- + -ait.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: il pleut → il pleuvait. il neige → il neigeait. il y a → il y avait.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Use past time phrases to signal the imperfect: hier (yesterday), l'été dernier (last summer), pendant les vacances (during the holidays).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Change il fait → il faisait, il pleut → il pleuvait, il neige → il neigeait, il y a → il y avait. Use past time phrases to signal the tense.

worked_examples.question: Translate to French: 'Last summer it was hot but tomorrow it's going to rain.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: 'Last summer' = L'été dernier. 'it was hot' = past weather → imperfect: il faisait chaud.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: 'but' = mais. 'tomorrow' = demain. 'it's going to rain' = near future: il va pleuvoir.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: L'été dernier, il faisait chaud mais demain il va pleuvoir.

bronze.question: Match the French weather expressions to the English meaning
Match the French travel problem and tourist office vocabulary to the English meaning
Complete the weather sentences with the correct word
sentence_parts: chaud en Espagne. En hiver, il
à la montagne. Aujourd'hui, il y a du

gaps.correct_explain: il fait chaud = it's hot. Weather uses il fait + adjective.

wrong.a: il a chaud means 'he is hot' (a person). For weather, use il fait chaud.
wrong.est: il est chaud is not used for weather. Use il fait chaud.

wrong.pleut: il pleut = it rains. For snow at the mountains in winter, you need neige.
wrong.neigeait: neigeait is the imperfect (past). The sentence uses the present tense, so you need neige.

gaps.rule: Weather pattern — il y a du + noun
gaps.correct_explain: il y a du soleil = it's sunny (literally 'there is sun').

wrong.vent: il y a du vent means it's windy, not sunny. You need soleil.
wrong.chaud: chaud goes with il fait, not il y a du. Use soleil.

bronze.question: Complete the travel problem sentences
sentence_parts: vol est annulé. Je cherche l'office

gaps.correct_explain: mon is the masculine singular possessive adjective. Le passeport is masculine.

wrong.ma: ma is for feminine nouns. Le passeport is masculine, so you need mon.
wrong.mes: mes is plural. Passeport is singular, so you need mon.

gaps.rule: Possessive adjective — masculine singular (at sentence start)
gaps.correct_explain: Mon (capitalised at start of sentence) is correct. Le vol is masculine.

wrong.Ma: Ma is for feminine nouns. Le vol is masculine, so you need Mon.
wrong.Mes: Mes is plural. Vol is singular, so you need Mon.

gaps.correct_explain: l'office du tourisme = the tourist office. Du is the contraction of de + le.

wrong.de: de le is not correct French — it contracts to du before a masculine noun.
wrong.des: des is the contraction of de + les (plural). Tourisme is singular masculine, so use du.

bronze.question: What does 'Il faisait beau et il y avait du soleil' mean?
options: The weather was nice and it was sunny
The weather is nice and it is sunny
The weather will be nice and it will be sunny
The weather was bad and it was cloudy

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly says 'Tomorrow it's going to snow' in the near future?

bronze.source_text: J'aime l'Espagne parce qu'il fait beau et il y a du soleil. Je déteste l'Angleterre parce qu'il pleut souvent.
model_answers: I like Spain because the weather is nice and it's sunny. I hate England because it often rains.
I like Spain because it's nice weather and it's sunny. I hate England because it rains often.
hints: il fait beau = the weather is nice

silver.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
silver.english: Last summer, it was very hot and it was sunny every day.

gaps.correct_explain: faisait is the imperfect of faire. Past weather descriptions use the imperfect: il faisait chaud.

wrong.fait: fait is the present tense. The time phrase l'été dernier (last summer) signals the past, so you need the imperfect: faisait.
wrong.fera: fera is the simple future. L'été dernier is past, so you need faisait.

gaps.rule: Imperfect — il y a → il y avait
gaps.correct_explain: il y avait is the imperfect of il y a. It means 'there was'.

wrong.a: il y a is the present tense. Past weather requires the imperfect: il y avait.
wrong.aura: il y aura is the simple future. L'été dernier requires the past: il y avait.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Hier, il fait beau mais aujourd'hui il pleut.
silver.explanation: Hier (yesterday) requires a past tense. Il fait is present. You need the imperfect: il faisait beau.
silver.translation: Yesterday, the weather was nice but today it's raining.

silver.question: Build the sentence in French
silver.english: I like France because the weather is nice and it's sunny.

distractor_labels.faisait: wrong tense — faisait is the imperfect (past), but this sentence is in the present tense

silver.source_text: In summer, the weather is nice in Spain but in winter it rains a lot. I prefer to travel by train because it's cheaper than the plane.
model_answers: En été, il fait beau en Espagne mais en hiver il pleut beaucoup. Je préfère voyager en train parce que c'est moins cher que l'avion.

model_answers: L'hiver dernier, il faisait très froid et il neigeait tous les jours. L'été prochain, il va faire beau et je vais voyager au Portugal en avion parce que j'adore le soleil.

gold.question: Build the sentence in French
gold.english: Tomorrow it will be sunny but next week it will rain.

distractor_labels.a: wrong tense — a (il y a) is the present, but you need the simple future il y aura
distractor_labels.avait: wrong tense — avait is the imperfect (past), but demain signals the future
distractor_labels.pleut: wrong tense — pleut is the present, but la semaine prochaine requires the future: pleuvra

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a tourist information office in France. You need help after losing your passport and want to find out about the local weather and places to visit.

bullets.prompt: Greet the assistant and explain that you have lost your passport.
bullets.model_answer: Bonjour! J'ai perdu mon passeport. Pouvez-vous m'aider, s'il vous plaît?
bullets.note: greeting + j'ai perdu (passé composé) + polite request (Pouvez-vous m'aider?)

bullets.prompt: Ask what the weather is going to be like tomorrow.
bullets.note: quel temps va-t-il faire — near future weather question

bullets.prompt: Ask for a map of the area and information about local monuments.
bullets.model_answer: Avez-vous une carte de la région et des renseignements sur les monuments historiques?
bullets.note: Avez-vous (polite question) + une carte de la région + des renseignements sur

bullets.prompt: Say what the weather was like on your last holiday and give your opinion.
bullets.model_answer: L'année dernière, il faisait très chaud et il y avait du soleil tous les jours. C'était fantastique!
bullets.note: imperfect weather (faisait, il y avait) + time phrase + opinion (c'était)
